name: The magicians of Egypt
charge: Withstanding Moses with their enchantments, and hardening Pharaoh in his refusal
summary: The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh and Aaron his prophet, and it was Aaron’s rod that became a serpent and swallowed up the rods of the magicians. They matched the blood and the frogs with their enchantments, but could only add to the plagues and never lift one. At the lice they could not, and told Pharaoh it was the finger of God; at the boils they could not stand before Moses, because the boil was upon them. Every plague mocked a god of Egypt, and the magicians served what was being mocked.
offenseFull: The Lord told Moses that he had made him a god to Pharaoh, with Aaron his brother as his prophet (Exodus 7:1). It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent; a great many people still say it was Moses holding the rod, because they do not read the account. Then Pharaoh called the wise men and the sorcerers, and the magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments, and every man cast down his rod, and they became serpents (Exodus 7:10-11). What they did was witchcraft, which the law names among the abominations for which the nations were cast out, and which is not to be suffered to live in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10-12; Exodus 22:18). There was real spiritual power at work; some of them dealt with Satan on a high level.

Mark the limit of the craft: they could copy a plague and they could never lift one. They turned water into blood and could not turn it back clear, so the fish still died and the river still stank and the Egyptians could not drink (Exodus 7:22). They brought up frogs on the land of Egypt and could not take away a single frog, so that Pharaoh had to send for Moses and entreat the Lord, and not Heqet, to have them destroyed (Exodus 8:7-8). Every imitation added to the affliction of their own country and handed the king a reason to refuse, and the record gives that reason each time: Pharaoh’s heart was hardened and he did not listen to them, as the Lord had said.
judgmentFull: Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods before the contest had properly begun (Exodus 7:12). Then the plagues came down on the very things the magicians served: the river to blood mocked Sobek, the god of the rivers; the frogs mocked Heqet; the lice and the biting flies mocked Beelzebub, the lord of flies and uncleanness; the murrain mocked Hathor; the boils mocked Sekhmet, the goddess of health; the hail and the fire mocked the sky and the earth; and the darkness mocked the sun god, for the Lord executed judgment against all the gods of Egypt (Exodus 12:12; Numbers 33:4).

At the third plague the craft ran out. The magicians tried with their enchantments to bring forth lice out of the dust and could not, and they told Pharaoh that this was the finger of God (Exodus 8:18-19). At the sixth they could not so much as stand in the room before Moses, because the boil was upon the magicians and upon all the Egyptians (Exodus 9:11). The men who claim now that none of this ever happened refuse it for the same reason: to admit it is to admit that the idols they call gods and goddesses were powerless before the God of Israel, and that those idols do not exist at all. Paul names the two and gives the standing sentence on every imitator after them: as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so these also resist the truth, but they shall proceed no further, for their folly shall be made manifest to all men (2 Timothy 3:8-9).

text.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the Lord had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.
There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord: and because of these abominations the Lord thy God doth drive them out from before thee.
Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
And the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them; as the Lord had said.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Intreat the Lord, that he may take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may do sacrifice unto the Lord.
For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.

For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the Lord.
For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast.
Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.
And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boil was upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians.
Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith.
But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was.
And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the Lord had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.
For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.
And he hardened Pharaoh’s heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

And they did so; for Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast.
Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as the Lord had said.
And the Lord said unto Moses and unto Aaron, Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the heaven in the sight of Pharaoh.
And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.
And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast.
And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boil was upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians.
